headline: The Taxis & Rideshare Master 20
threshold: By Lesson 20, you can teach a companion how local taxis and ride apps work and why, sort out a wrong car or a strike and turn down unsafe offers, lead a tired group and change your tone for each listener, handle and report incidents and emergencies, and write formal claims and ride messages in Spanish.

lessons.title: Explain Sitio Taxis to a Colleague New to Mexico City
lessons.objective: Explain how sitio, street and app taxis differ here and why you choose each one, then check her teach-back.

words.en: the sitio taxi (dispatched from a base)
words.note: Mexico: a taxi you request from a fixed stand or by phone.
Mexico: a cab you hail on the street; the LIBRE sign means it's available.
Mexico City: the driver's official card displayed inside the cab.
Mexico City term for the official taxi paint colors.
Mexico: the starting amount on the meter.
Mexico: dispatchers and drivers call each taxi una unidad.

words.en: First I'll explain the three kinds of taxi here.
words.es: Primero te explico los tres tipos de taxi que hay aquí.
words.note: Informal (tú), colleague to colleague.

words.en: Hailing a taxi on the street looks easy, but it's not always a good idea.
words.es: Parar un taxi en la calle parece fácil, pero no siempre conviene.

words.en: I order a sitio taxi because I know which base it comes from.
words.es: Pido un taxi de sitio porque sé de qué base sale.

words.en: Then you check that the driver's ID card is on display.
words.es: Luego revisas que el tarjetón esté a la vista.
words.note: Revisar que takes the subjunctive: esté.

words.en: With the app you see the price beforehand; that's why I use it.
words.es: Con la app ves el precio antes; por eso la uso.

words.en: Can you explain it to me now, in your own words?
words.es: ¿Me lo explicas ahora tú, con tus propias palabras?
words.note: Informal (tú).

words.en: Could you give me the taxi stand's phone number, please?
words.es: ¿Me podría dar el teléfono del sitio, por favor?
words.note: Formal (usted), to hotel staff.

lessons.speaking: You are the experienced traveler, and the AI is Valeria, a colleague new to Mexico City: explain how sitio, street and app taxis differ and when you choose each, using primero, luego, porque and por eso, then have her explain it back and correct her gently.

grammar.focus: Connectors for sequence and cause (primero, luego, porque, por eso)

examples.es: Primero llamas al sitio y luego te mandan una unidad.
examples.en: First you call the taxi stand, and then they send you a cab.

examples.es: El taxi de sitio sale de una base, por eso sabes quién te lleva.
examples.en: The sitio taxi comes from a base; that's why you know who's driving you.

lessons.title: Read the Airport Fixed-Fare Board for Your Group
lessons.objective: Read the official airport fare board and explain to your group what the fixed fare includes and what it leaves out.

words.note: Madrid's inner ring road; read the board to see how it marks the fixed-fare zone.
Spain's usual word for an extra charge on a taxi fare.
Spain word; Mexico says la cajuela.
Se paga aparte = it's charged on top.

words.en: According to the official board, the fixed fare is 33 euros.
words.es: Según el cartel oficial, la tarifa fija es de 33 euros.

words.en: If you're going inside the M-30, you pay the fixed price.
words.es: Si vais dentro de la M-30, se paga el precio fijo.
words.note: Informal plural (vosotros), used in Spain.

words.en: Your hotel is outside the zone; it's charged by the meter.
words.es: Vuestro hotel queda fuera de la zona; se cobra por taxímetro.
words.note: Informal plural (vosotros).

words.en: Look, it says here there's a minimum fare outside the zone.
words.es: Mirad, aquí pone que fuera de la zona hay una tarifa mínima.
words.note: Spain: aquí pone = it says here.

words.en: Excuse me, is the luggage surcharge included in the fixed fare?
words.es: Perdone, ¿el suplemento de equipaje va incluido en la tarifa fija?
words.note: Formal (usted), to the attendant.

words.en: Could you tell me exactly where the fixed-fare zone ends?
words.es: ¿Me podría decir dónde termina exactamente la zona de tarifa fija?
words.note: Formal (usted).

words.en: If the board doesn't make it clear, we'll ask the attendant.
words.es: Si el cartel no lo aclara, se lo preguntamos al encargado.

lessons.speaking: You are reading the fare board at the Madrid-Barajas rank, and the AI plays attendant Paco and your cousins Inés and Joaquín: explain what the fixed fare covers and what it leaves out, using se paga, se cobra and si + present, and quote every figure según el cartel oficial.

grammar.focus: Impersonal se; si + present for general truths (se paga al llegar, si vas al centro la tarifa es fija)

examples.es: Según el cartel oficial, se paga la tarifa fija si el destino está dentro de la M-30.
examples.en: According to the official board, you pay the fixed fare if the destination is inside the M-30.

examples.es: Si el hotel está fuera de la zona, se cobra por taxímetro.
examples.en: If the hotel is outside the zone, it's charged by the meter.

lessons.title: Train a Classmate to Verify Her Rideshare in Bogotá
lessons.objective: Coach a newcomer step by step to check the plate, driver and route in the app, then have her teach it back.

words.note: Feminine: sospechosa.

words.en: Open it and look for the driver's details.
words.es: Ábrela y busca los datos del conductor.
words.note: Informal (tú); la = la app. Pronoun attaches to positive commands.

words.en: Look at the plate and compare it with the one on the screen.
words.es: Mira la placa y compárala con la de la pantalla.
words.note: Informal (tú).

words.en: Also check the color and model; verify them before you get in.
words.es: Revisa también el color y el modelo; verifícalos antes de subirte.

words.en: If anything doesn't match, don't accept it, and cancel it.
words.es: Si algo no coincide, no lo aceptes y cancélalo.
words.note: Negative command: pronoun goes before the verb (no lo aceptes).

words.en: Share your real-time location with a trusted contact.
words.es: Comparte tu ubicación en tiempo real con un contacto de confianza.

words.en: Hi, can you confirm who the ride is for, please?
words.es: Buenas, ¿me confirma para quién es el servicio, por favor?
words.note: Formal (usted), to the driver. Let him say the name first.

words.en: Now you explain it to me, step by step.
words.es: Ahora explícamelo tú, paso a paso.
words.note: Informal (tú).

lessons.speaking: You are training the AI, Lucía, a newcomer in Bogotá, to verify her rideshare: walk her through checking the plate, driver and route in the app with commands like ábrela, compruébalo and no lo aceptes, then have her teach the steps back to you.

grammar.focus: Commands with object pronouns (ábrela, compruébalo, no lo aceptes)

examples.es: Abre la app y revisa la placa; compruébala antes de subirte.
examples.en: Open the app and check the plate; double-check it before you get in.

examples.es: Si los datos no coinciden, no lo aceptes; cancélalo desde la app.
examples.en: If the details don't match, don't accept it; cancel it from the app.

lessons.title: Read the Window Rate Card Before a Buenos Aires Ride
lessons.objective: Read a taxi's posted rate card and explain the night and luggage supplements to a friend before you set off.

words.note: Argentine term for the official table of taxi rates.
Buenos Aires: drivers and passengers call the taxi meter el reloj.
Argentina: the meter counts up in fichas.
Argentine usage for a supplement added to the fare.
Argentina; Mexico says la maleta.
Argentina: a travel bag or holdall.
Feminine: vencida (la tarjeta está vencida).

words.en: Mariela, before getting in, look at the card on the window.
words.es: Mariela, antes de subir, fijate en la tarjeta del vidrio.
words.note: Informal Argentine vos command: fijate (not fíjate).

words.en: According to the rate card, the night rate applies from 22 to 6.
words.es: Según la tarjeta de tarifas, la nocturna rige de 22 a 6.

words.en: There's an extra charge for the suitcases, according to the card.
words.es: Por las valijas hay un adicional, según dice la tarjeta.

words.en: Excuse me, is the card current, or is there a new fare schedule?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿la tarjeta está vigente o hay un cuadro tarifario nuevo?
words.note: Formal (usted), to the driver.

words.en: Could you show me the current fare schedule before we leave?
words.es: ¿Me podría mostrar el cuadro tarifario actual antes de salir?
words.note: Formal (usted).

words.en: Before we set off, would you start the meter, please?
words.es: Antes de arrancar, ¿pone el reloj, por favor?
words.note: Formal (usted). Arrancar = to set off (in a vehicle).

words.en: If the card is out of date, we have to ask before setting off.
words.es: Si la tarjeta está vencida, hay que preguntar antes de arrancar.

lessons.speaking: You are on a Palermo corner with your friend Mariela, and the AI plays driver Néstor Gallo and Mariela: read the taxi's rate card aloud and explain the night and luggage supplements según la tarjeta de tarifas, using antes de / después de + infinitive and hay que.

grammar.focus: Antes de / después de + infinitive; hay que (antes de subir, hay que mirar la tarifa)

examples.es: Antes de subir, hay que mirar la tarjeta de tarifas.
examples.en: Before getting in, you have to look at the rate card.

examples.es: Después de cargar las valijas, hay que preguntar si el adicional sigue vigente.
examples.en: After loading the suitcases, you have to ask whether the extra charge still applies.

lessons.title: Booked an SUV, a Sedan Came: Propose a Second Car
lessons.objective: Explain what you booked and what actually arrived, and propose a fair fix for five people and eight bags.

words.note: Colombian usage; Mexico says la cajuela.
Colombian usage for a car's roof rack.
Common in Colombia for a customer service agent; la asesora for a woman.
Informal, very common in Colombia; also la captura de pantalla.

words.en: I booked an SUV for 5 people and 8 suitcases.
words.es: Reservé una camioneta para 5 personas y 8 maletas.

words.en: I thought an SUV was coming, not a sedan.
words.es: Yo pensaba que venía una camioneta, no un sedán.

words.en: When you arrived, we already had all the luggage outside.
words.es: Cuando usted llegó, ya teníamos todo el equipaje afuera.
words.note: Formal: usted to the driver.

words.en: Could we order a second car for 2 people and the suitcases?
words.es: ¿Podríamos pedir un segundo carro para 2 personas y las maletas?

words.en: Don Jhon Fredy, it's not your fault; it was the app.
words.es: Don Jhon Fredy, no es culpa suya; fue la app.
words.note: Formal and polite; paisas often use both first names.

words.en: I'm sending you a screenshot of the confirmation right now.
words.es: Le mando un pantallazo de la confirmación ahora mismo.
words.note: Formal, to the support agent.

words.en: Could you refund me the extra cost of the second car?
words.es: ¿Me podrían devolver el sobrecosto del segundo carro?

words.en: We have a flight at 3, so we can't wait long.
words.es: Tenemos vuelo a las 3, así que no podemos esperar mucho.

lessons.speaking: You are leading a family group of five, and the AI is driver Jhon Fredy, who arrived in a sedan: explain what you booked with reservé and yo pensaba que, then propose a fair fix with ¿podríamos...? before your flight.

grammar.focus: Preterite vs imperfect; conditional for the proposal (reservé una camioneta, yo pensaba que..., ¿podríamos pedir otro coche?)

examples.es: Reservé una camioneta, pero llegó un sedán pequeño.
examples.en: I booked an SUV, but a small sedan arrived.

examples.es: ¿Podríamos dividirnos en dos carros?
examples.en: Could we split into two cars?

lessons.title: Taxi Strike in Barcelona: Compare Your Options
lessons.objective: Compare bus, rideshare and hotel shuttle options during a strike and choose a realistic plan for your group.

words.note: Spain: the reduced service that must run during a strike.
Changing from one line or vehicle to another.
Spain's term for app-booked cars with a driver (Uber, Cabify); say un VTC.
Spain usage; Latin America often says el trancón or el embotellamiento.

words.en: Arnau, the bus is going to take longer than the rideshare.
words.es: Arnau, el autobús va a tardar más que el VTC.
words.note: Informal, to your colleague.

words.en: With the strike, a rideshare will be more expensive than usual.
words.es: Con la huelga, un VTC será más caro de lo normal.

words.en: If we leave at 2, we'll get to boarding with time to spare.
words.es: Si salimos a las 2, llegaremos con margen al embarque.

words.en: Excuse me, what time does the hotel shuttle leave?
words.es: Disculpe, ¿a qué hora sale el traslado del hotel?
words.note: Formal, to the concierge.

words.en: Don't worry, we'll check the price in the app.
words.es: No se preocupe, el precio lo miramos en la app.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: The shuttle is slower, but it's the most reliable option.
words.es: El traslado es más lento, pero es la opción más fiable.

words.en: Are we going to take the bus or order a rideshare?
words.es: ¿Vamos a coger el bus o pedimos un VTC?
words.note: Informal. Coger is neutral in Spain; avoid it in Latin America.

words.en: In case there's a traffic jam, we're going to have a backup plan.
words.es: Por si hay atasco, vamos a tener un plan B.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Montse, the hotel concierge: ask about the bus, rideshare and hotel shuttle to a 4 p.m. ferry, compare them with más... que and va a tardar, and choose a plan using the future (saldremos, llegaremos).

grammar.focus: Future and ir a; comparisons (el autobús va a tardar más que el coche, será más barato)

examples.es: El autobús va a tardar más que el coche.
examples.en: The bus is going to take longer than the car.

examples.es: Con la huelga, el bus irá más lleno que de costumbre.
examples.en: With the strike, the bus will be more crowded than usual.

lessons.title: Police Checkpoint: Answer the Officer's Questions
lessons.objective: Narrate your trip so far and give your passport, flight and address numbers clearly to a police officer.

words.note: Chile's national police; el carabinero for a man.
Use it to answer the purpose question: Vine de turismo.
Chilean usage; Mexico says la placa.

words.en: Sergeant, may I take my passport out of my backpack?
words.es: Sargento, ¿puedo sacar el pasaporte de la mochila?
words.note: Formal. Ask before reaching into a bag and keep your hands visible.

words.en: I took the taxi at the airport about 20 minutes ago.
words.es: Tomé el taxi en el aeropuerto hace unos 20 minutos.

words.en: I arrived on flight LA 801 from Lima this morning.
words.es: Llegué en el vuelo LA 801 desde Lima esta mañana.
words.note: Read flight numbers in pairs or digit by digit: ocho, cero, uno.

words.en: I came as a tourist and I'm staying 5 nights.
words.es: Vine de turismo y me quedo 5 noches.

words.en: My passport is A5382147; I'll repeat it slowly for you.
words.es: Mi pasaporte es el A5382147; se lo repito despacio.
words.note: Say letters clearly: A, then each digit one by one.

words.en: I'm staying in Providencia; I have the exact address here.
words.es: Me alojo en Providencia; aquí tengo la dirección exacta.

words.en: Excuse me, could you repeat that more slowly?
words.es: Perdone, ¿me lo puede repetir más despacio?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: I don't know the driver; I took the official airport taxi.
words.es: No conozco al conductor; tomé el taxi oficial del aeropuerto.

lessons.speaking: You are the passenger, and the AI is Sargento Paula Henríquez at a checkpoint: stay calm, ask before reaching for documents, narrate your trip in the preterite (salimos, tomé, llegué) and give your passport, flight and address numbers clearly.

grammar.focus: Preterite narration; numbers under pressure (salimos del aeropuerto a las nueve, el pasaporte termina en 47)

examples.es: Salimos del aeropuerto a las 9 y vinimos directo.
examples.en: We left the airport at 9 and came straight here.

examples.es: El pasaporte termina en 47.
examples.en: The passport ends in 47.

lessons.title: Saying No: Seven People in a Five-Seat Car
lessons.objective: Turn down a driver's offer to squeeze everyone in and convince your group to split into two cars.

words.note: Colombian usage for a seat in a vehicle: un carro de 5 puestos.
Colombian: an available place in a vehicle. ¿Hay cupo?
Colombian term for carrying more passengers than the seats allow.
Colombian usage.
La agente de tránsito for a woman.
Colombia's compulsory traffic accident insurance; say it as one word: el soat.

words.en: Don't get in yet; we're going to order another car.
words.es: No se suban todavía; vamos a pedir otro carro.
words.note: Plural ustedes command, to the group.

words.en: Thanks, don Wilmer, but 7 people don't fit in 5 seats.
words.es: Gracias, don Wilmer, pero 7 personas no caben en 5 puestos.
words.note: Formal and polite, to the driver.

words.en: I don't recommend anyone riding without a seat belt.
words.es: No recomiendo que nadie viaje sin cinturón de seguridad.

words.en: Sebas, I don't recommend we take the risk to save 10 minutes.
words.es: Sebas, no recomiendo que nos arriesguemos por ahorrar 10 minutos.
words.note: Informal, to Sebastián.

words.en: Please don't sit on anyone's lap.
words.es: No se sienten en las piernas de nadie, por favor.
words.note: Plural ustedes command.

words.en: Let's split up: 4 in this car and 3 in the other.
words.es: Nos dividimos: 4 en este carro y 3 en el otro.

words.en: I'd rather we all get there safely, even if it's later.
words.es: Prefiero que lleguemos todos bien, aunque sea más tarde.

words.en: Could you call a fellow driver for the rest of the group?
words.es: ¿Usted podría llamar a un compañero para el resto del grupo?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are a wedding guest, and the AI plays driver Wilmer and the bride's brother Sebastián: politely refuse the offer to fit seven in five seats and convince Sebastián to split into two cars, using negative commands (no se suban) and no recomiendo que + subjunctive.

grammar.focus: Negative commands; subjunctive after no recomiendo que (no se suban, no recomiendo que vayamos sin cinturón)

examples.es: No se suban todos al mismo carro.
examples.en: Don't all get into the same car.

examples.es: No recomiendo que vayamos apretados en un solo carro.
examples.en: I don't recommend that we ride squeezed into one car.

lessons.title: Feedback for Your Conference Driver After a Rough Day
lessons.objective: Give a hired driver clear, respectful feedback about lateness and phone use, and agree on tomorrow's plan.

words.note: Common in Mexican workplaces; in casual talk people also say los comentarios.

words.en: the car park, the parking lot
words.note: Mexican usage for a parking area.
Guadalajara's main ring road; locals just say el Periférico.

words.en: Don Ernesto, do you have a minute to talk?
words.es: Don Ernesto, ¿tiene un minuto para platicar?
words.note: Formal. Platicar is the everyday Mexican word for chatting or talking.

words.en: I really value your work; that's why I'm telling you.
words.es: Valoro mucho su trabajo, por eso se lo digo.
words.note: Formal. Say this before the criticism so the feedback lands as respect.

words.en: I'd prefer that you arrive at 7:45 tomorrow, 15 minutes early.
words.es: Prefiero que mañana llegue a las 7:45, 15 minutos antes.
words.note: Prefiero que + subjunctive: llegue, not llega.

words.en: I ask that you not use your phone while you drive.
words.es: Le pido que no use el teléfono mientras maneja.
words.note: Formal. Le pido que + subjunctive is firm but polite.

words.en: If you need to answer, I ask you to pull over first.
words.es: Si necesita contestar, le pido que se estacione primero.

words.en: If you're going to be late, please let me know beforehand.
words.es: Si se va a retrasar, le pido que me avise antes.

words.en: I want all of us to get to the venue safely.
words.es: Quiero que todos lleguemos seguros a la sede.

words.en: Is it all right with you if we leave the hotel at 8?
words.es: ¿Le parece bien que salgamos del hotel a las 8?
words.note: Le parece bien que + subjunctive invites agreement instead of giving an order.

lessons.speaking: You are the team lead, and the AI is Don Ernesto, your hired conference driver: give respectful feedback on his lateness and texting while driving, then agree on tomorrow's pickup using prefiero que..., le pido que... and ¿le parece bien que...?

grammar.focus: Present subjunctive after wishes and recommendations (prefiero que llegue antes, le pido que no use el teléfono)

examples.es: Le recomiendo que deje el celular en la guantera.
examples.en: I recommend that you leave your phone in the glove box.

examples.es: Ojalá que mañana no haya tanto tráfico en el Periférico.
examples.en: Hopefully there won't be so much traffic on the Periférico tomorrow.

lessons.title: Doorman and Driver Both Claim Your Ride
lessons.objective: Report what each side said and settle who takes you, without blaming either of them.

words.note: Rioplatense word for sidewalk.
Short for el cordón de la vereda in Uruguay and Argentina.
Always la pareja, even for a man: Diego es mi pareja.
Rioplatense: recién llegó means she just arrived.

words.en: Calm down, please; it was a misunderstanding and nobody is to blame.
words.es: Calma, por favor; fue un malentendido y nadie tiene la culpa.

words.en: Walter told me he had already called a radio taxi.
words.es: Walter me dijo que ya había llamado un radio taxi.
words.note: Reported speech: dijo que + pluperfect (había llamado) for the earlier action.

words.en: Andrea said the booking was in Diego's name.
words.es: Andrea dijo que la reserva estaba a nombre de Diego.

words.en: I didn't know my partner had ordered a car.
words.es: Yo no sabía que mi pareja había pedido un auto.
words.note: Uruguayans say el auto for a car.

words.en: While Walter was calling the taxi, Diego was ordering the car on the app.
words.es: Mientras Walter llamaba el taxi, Diego pedía el auto por la app.
words.note: Two imperfects with mientras for actions happening at the same time.

words.en: Diego, did you order a car on the app?
words.es: Diego, ¿vos pediste un auto por la app?
words.note: Informal. Uruguayans use vos with friends and partners.

words.en: Walter, sorry for the trouble; can you cancel the radio taxi?
words.es: Walter, disculpe la molestia; ¿puede cancelar el radio taxi?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Neither of you did anything wrong.
words.es: Ninguno de los dos hizo nada mal.

lessons.speaking: You are the hotel guest, and the AI plays doorman Walter and app driver Andrea, arguing at the curb: calmly report what each one said, using dijo que ya había... and estaba esperando, then decide who takes you without blaming either of them.

grammar.focus: Reported speech; imperfect for background (el portero dijo que ya había llamado, usted estaba esperando)

examples.es: El portero dijo que el taxi ya venía en camino.
examples.en: The doorman said the taxi was already on its way.

examples.es: La conductora explicó que estaba esperando en la vereda.
examples.en: The driver explained that she was waiting on the sidewalk.

lessons.title: Keep a Tired Group Going in a 2 a.m. Taxi Queue
lessons.objective: Encourage a tired group, commit to a clear plan, and keep everyone together until the last car leaves.

words.note: Por tandas = in waves, a few at a time.
In Quito, el valle means the Cumbayá–Tumbaco or Los Chillos suburbs.
¡Ánimo! on its own means Hang in there!

words.en: the small hours, the early morning

words.note: Juntas if the whole group is women.
Ecuadorian: ya mismo means soon, not right this second.

words.en: Hang in there, we're almost out; not long now.
words.es: Ánimo, ya casi salimos; falta poco.
words.note: Informal, to the whole group.

words.en: I'll stay with the bags until the last car leaves.
words.es: Yo me quedaré con las maletas hasta que salga el último carro.

words.en: Camila, I get it; it's been a really long day.
words.es: Camila, te entiendo; ha sido un día larguísimo.
words.note: Informal: tú between fellow volunteers.

words.en: Nobody will leave alone; we'll go out in groups of 3.
words.es: Nadie se irá solo; saldremos en grupos de 3.

words.en: Don Rubén, how many cars will come in the next wave?
words.es: Don Rubén, ¿cuántos carros vendrán en la próxima tanda?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: When you get there, each of you will check in on the group chat.
words.es: Al llegar, cada uno avisará en el chat del grupo.

words.en: We'll wait together here, at the meeting point.
words.es: Esperaremos juntos aquí, en el punto de encuentro.

words.en: Thanks for your patience; tomorrow we'll start later.
words.es: Gracias por la paciencia; mañana empezaremos más tarde.

lessons.speaking: You are the leader of a volunteer group, and the AI is Camila, a tired and frustrated volunteer: encourage her, explain the plan for the cars to the valley, and promise to keep everyone together using the future (me quedaré, saldremos) and ánimo, ya casi...

grammar.focus: Future for commitments; encouragement register (yo me quedaré con las maletas, ya casi salimos)

examples.es: Yo pediré los carros y tú revisarás la lista, Camila.
examples.en: I'll ask for the cars and you'll check the list, Camila.

examples.es: Saldremos en la segunda tanda; ya casi nos toca.
examples.en: We'll leave in the second wave; it's almost our turn.

lessons.title: One Pickup, Three Listeners: Dispatcher, Friend, Manager
lessons.objective: Explain the same pickup change to a dispatcher, a friend and a hotel manager, using the right register for each.

words.note: Spain usage for picking up a passenger.
Spain usage for the taxi company's phone line.
Spain usage for the gate or garage remote.
Spain usage.
Use la responsable de turno for a woman.
Informal Spain usage: getting up at the crack of dawn.
In Spain, a WhatsApp voice note is simply called an audio.
Informal Spain, between friends only.

words.en: Good morning, I'd like to move an airport pickup earlier.
words.es: Buenos días, quisiera adelantar una recogida para el aeropuerto.
words.note: Formal. Quisiera sounds softer than quiero.

words.en: Would it be possible to move the pickup up to 5:15?
words.es: ¿Sería posible adelantar la recogida a las 5:15?
words.note: Formal softener for a request.

words.en: Nacho, mate, change of plans: they're picking us up at 5:15.
words.es: Nacho, tío, cambio de planes: nos recogen a las 5:15.
words.note: Informal, to a friend.

words.en: I'll send you a voice message with the details, OK?
words.es: Te mando un audio con los detalles, ¿vale?
words.note: Informal. ¿Vale? is the Spanish way to say OK?

words.en: Mr. Bellver, excuse me, I'd like to ask you a favor.
words.es: Señor Bellver, disculpe, quisiera pedirle un favor.
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Would it be possible to let the driver into the inner courtyard?
words.es: ¿Sería posible dejar pasar al conductor al patio interior?
words.note: Personal a: al conductor, because he is a person.

words.en: I'll pass you the taxi's plate number as soon as I have it.
words.es: La matrícula del taxi se la paso en cuanto la tenga.
words.note: Formal: se la paso = I'll give it to you (usted).

words.en: Could you confirm the pickup for me by email, please?
words.es: ¿Podría confirmarme la recogida por correo, por favor?
words.note: Formal.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI plays dispatcher Amparo, your friend Nacho and duty manager Sr. Bellver: explain the earlier pickup to each one, using usted with quisiera and ¿sería posible...? for Amparo and Sr. Bellver, and tú with Nacho.

grammar.focus: Usted / tú switching; softeners (quisiera, ¿sería posible...?)

examples.es: ¿Sería posible que el conductor entrara en el patio?
examples.en: Would it be possible for the driver to come into the courtyard?

examples.es: Nacho, ¿puedes bajar a las 5? Ya te mando la matrícula.
examples.en: Nacho, can you come down at 5? I'll send you the plate number.

lessons.title: A Door Hits a Cyclist: Report the Incident
lessons.objective: Narrate exactly what happened, minute by minute, to the driver, the cyclist and the ride company.

words.note: Same form for a woman: la ciclista.
Spain usage. Latin America says la ciclovía.
The part of the street where traffic moves, as opposed to la acera.

words.en: At 6:10 the car stopped on Betis Street.
words.es: A las 6:10 el coche paró en la calle Betis.

words.en: At that moment a cyclist was riding by in the bike lane.
words.es: En ese momento pasaba un ciclista por el carril bici.
words.note: Imperfect (pasaba) for the background action, preterite for what happened next.

words.en: Right after that, the door hit him on the elbow.
words.es: Justo después, la puerta le dio en el codo.

words.en: Mr. Ortega, did you hurt your arm?
words.es: Señor Ortega, ¿se ha hecho daño en el brazo?
words.note: Formal. In Spain the present perfect is normal for something that just happened.

words.en: Rocío, did you see the bike coming before you opened the door?
words.es: Rocío, ¿tú viste venir la bici antes de abrir?
words.note: Informal, to a friend.

words.en: Antonio, can you confirm what time the car stopped?
words.es: Antonio, ¿me confirma a qué hora paró el coche?
words.note: Formal: usted with the driver, even when you use his first name.

words.en: I'm writing to report an incident with the door.
words.es: Les escribo para informar de un incidente con la puerta.
words.note: Formal, for the ride company's report form.

words.en: Manuel has a scrape on his elbow, but he's on his feet.
words.es: Manuel tiene una rozadura en el codo, pero está de pie.

lessons.speaking: You are the passenger, and the AI is driver Antonio, then cyclist Manuel, then the app's support agent: tell what happened minute by minute, using the preterite and imperfect with time markers like a las 6:10, justo después and en ese momento.

grammar.focus: Past narration with time markers (a las seis y diez, justo después, en ese momento)

examples.es: A las 6:10, Rocío abrió la puerta del lado de la calzada.
examples.en: At 6:10, Rocío opened the door on the traffic side.

examples.es: En ese momento pasó Manuel en bici y la puerta lo rozó.
examples.en: At that moment Manuel rode past and the door grazed him.

lessons.title: Near Miss at the Curb: Talk It Through Without Blame
lessons.objective: Talk through a near miss with the driver and your nephew, and agree on a safer drop-off routine.

words.note: Peru and Chile usage for a bus stop.
In Peru, la pista is the street or road where cars drive.
Common in Peru for someone riding a motorbike.
In Peru traffic drives on the right, so this is usually the curb side.
Use the present tense for a past event: por poco te golpea = it nearly hit you.

words.en: That motorbike nearly hit you, Mateo!
words.es: ¡Por poco te golpea esa moto, Mateo!
words.note: Informal, to your nephew.

words.en: Something serious almost happened, but it's nobody's fault.
words.es: Casi pasa algo grave, pero no es culpa de nadie.

words.en: Mateo, you could have gotten hurt; always get out on the right.
words.es: Mateo, podrías haberte lastimado; siempre baja por la derecha.
words.note: Informal tú command (baja).

words.en: Mateo, what did you see from your seat before you opened the door?
words.es: Mateo, ¿qué viste tú desde el asiento antes de abrir?
words.note: An open question asks what happened without blaming anyone.

words.en: Mrs. Rosa, could you see the motorbike in the mirror?
words.es: Señora Rosa, ¿se veía la moto por el espejo?
words.note: Formal.

words.en: Mrs. Rosa, if you stop at the corner, we can get out more safely.
words.es: Señora Rosa, si para en la esquina, bajamos más seguros.
words.note: Formal. Si + present, then present for a routine.

words.en: If the car isn't stopped, nobody opens the door.
words.es: Si el carro no está detenido, nadie abre la puerta.

words.en: So we agree: we stop outside the lane and get out on the right.
words.es: Quedamos así: paramos fuera del carril y bajamos por la derecha.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveling uncle or aunt, and the AI is driver Rosa and your nephew Mateo: talk through what nearly happened without blaming anyone, using por poco, casi and podría haber, then agree on a safer drop-off routine with si paramos…, bajamos….

grammar.focus: Casi, por poco, podría haber; si clauses (por poco lo golpea una moto, si paramos en la esquina bajamos seguros)

examples.es: Por poco lo golpea una moto al bajar por la izquierda.
examples.en: A motorbike nearly hit him when he got out on the left.

examples.es: Si paramos fuera del carril exclusivo, Mateo baja seguro por la derecha.
examples.en: If we stop outside the bus lane, Mateo gets out safely on the right.

lessons.title: Driver Feels Ill at the Wheel: Pull Over and Call
lessons.objective: Get a sick driver to stop safely, call emergency services, and give your location and short updates.

words.note: Costa Rica usage. Mexico says el acotamiento.
In Costa Rica the Cruz Roja runs many ambulances.
In Costa Rica the emergency number is 911.

words.en: Mr. Gerardo, pull over slowly onto the shoulder, please.
words.es: Don Gerardo, oríllese despacio en el espaldón, por favor.
words.note: Formal. Orillarse means to pull over in Central America and Mexico.

words.en: Turn on the hazard lights and set the parking brake.
words.es: Ponga las luces de emergencia y el freno de mano.
words.note: Formal usted command.

words.en: If the pain continues, I'll call 911 right now.
words.es: Si el dolor sigue, llamaré al 911 ahora mismo.

words.en: Hello, it's an emergency: the driver has chest pain.
words.es: Buenas, es una emergencia: el conductor tiene dolor en el pecho.

words.en: We're on the shoulder of Route 27, heading toward San José.
words.es: Estamos en el espaldón de la Ruta 27, hacia San José.

words.en: He's conscious and breathing, but he's sweating a lot.
words.es: Él está consciente y respira, pero está sudando mucho.

words.en: Yes, I'll stay on the line and tell you if anything changes.
words.es: Sí, me quedo en línea y le aviso si algo cambia.

words.en: Mr. Gerardo, the ambulance is on its way; stay still here with me.
words.es: Don Gerardo, la ambulancia ya viene; quédese quieto conmigo.
words.note: Formal. Don + first name is respectful and warm.

lessons.speaking: You are the passenger, and the AI is driver Gerardo, then emergency operator Karla: get him onto the espaldón with usted commands like oríllese, call the emergency line, and give your location and short updates using si + present → future (si el dolor sigue, llamaré).

grammar.focus: Si + present → future; short phone commands (si se marea, paramos; quédese en línea)

examples.es: Si don Gerardo pierde el conocimiento, se lo diré de inmediato.
examples.en: If Mr. Gerardo loses consciousness, I'll tell you immediately.

examples.es: Quédese en línea y no cuelgue, por favor.
examples.en: Stay on the line and don't hang up, please.

lessons.title: Municipal Taxi Inspector Takes Your Statement
lessons.objective: Give a transport inspector a formal, step-by-step statement about an unlicensed driver, then review it and sign.

words.note: For a woman. A man is el inspector de tránsito.
In Panama people often call it the ATTT.

words.en: Ma'am, I was offered a taxi inside the terminal.
words.es: Licenciada, se me ofreció un taxi dentro de la terminal.
words.note: Licenciada is a respectful title for a university graduate, common in Panama.

words.en: I was charged 90 dollars in cash when we arrived.
words.es: Se me cobraron 90 dólares en efectivo al llegar.
words.note: With passive se, the verb is plural when the thing is plural: se cobraron 90 dólares.

words.en: According to the official sign, the fare was 30 dollars.
words.es: Según el letrero oficial, la tarifa era de 30 dólares.

words.en: The car had no taxi plate and no visible ID.
words.es: El vehículo no tenía placa de taxi ni credencial visible.

words.en: In what order would you like me to give you the details?
words.es: ¿En qué orden prefiere que le dé los datos?
words.note: Formal. Prefiere que takes the subjunctive (dé).

words.en: Could you read me the full statement before I sign?
words.es: ¿Me podría leer la declaración completa antes de firmar?

words.en: Excuse me, point 3 should say 4:20, not 4:00.
words.es: Disculpe, en el punto 3 debe decir 4:20, no 4:00.

words.en: Do I sign here and put the date below?
words.es: ¿Se firma aquí y se pone la fecha abajo?

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is inspector Licenciada Batista: give a formal, step-by-step statement about the unlicensed driver in the order she asks, using passive se (se me ofreció, se me cobró), then review the statement and sign it.

grammar.focus: Formal register; passive se for procedures (se me ofreció un taxi, se cobró el triple, se firma aquí)

examples.es: Se me ofreció un taxi en la zona de llegadas y se me cobró el triple.
examples.en: I was offered a taxi in the arrivals area and charged triple.

examples.es: La declaración se revisa, se corrige y se firma aquí.
examples.en: The statement is reviewed, corrected and signed here.

lessons.title: Write the Claim for a Suitcase Broken in the Trunk
lessons.objective: Write a clear, formal claim to a taxi company with trip details, the receipt, photos and a specific request.

words.note: Spain: the standard word for a formal complaint or claim.
Feminine noun that takes el in the singular because it starts with a stressed a.
Formal written word for damage to an object.
Spain: common word for a receipt or proof of payment.
Spain: official form that businesses must provide on request.
Standard formal sign-off for letters and emails.

words.en: I am writing to file a claim for damage to my suitcase.
words.es: Le escribo para presentar una reclamación por daños en mi maleta.
words.note: Formal written opening.

words.en: On May 14 I used a taxi from your cooperative in Málaga.
words.es: El 14 de mayo utilicé un taxi de su cooperativa en Málaga.

words.en: When closing the trunk, the driver hit my suitcase handle.
words.es: Al cerrar el maletero, el conductor golpeó el asa de mi maleta.

words.en: It should be noted that the receipt shows the wrong date.
words.es: Cabe señalar que el justificante indica una fecha errónea.

words.en: I attach the photos of the broken handle and the trip receipt.
words.es: Adjunto las fotografías del asa rota y el justificante del trayecto.

words.en: Therefore, I request that you refund me the cost of the repair.
words.es: Por lo tanto, solicito que me reembolsen el coste de la reparación.
words.note: Solicitar que takes the subjunctive.

words.en: I would appreciate a written reply within a reasonable time.
words.es: Les agradecería una respuesta por escrito en un plazo razonable.

words.en: I look forward to your reply.
words.es: Quedo a la espera de su respuesta.
words.note: Fixed formal closing line, used before the sign-off.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Elena Ruiz, customer service agent at the Málaga taxi cooperative: present your written claim about the suitcase handle and the receipt date, using adjunto, cabe señalar que and por lo tanto, and end with a specific request.

grammar.focus: Written register; report connectors (por lo tanto, cabe señalar que, adjunto)

examples.es: Cabe señalar que el justificante indica el 13 de mayo, no el 14.
examples.en: It should be noted that the receipt shows May 13, not May 14.

examples.es: Por lo tanto, solicito la corrección del justificante y el pago de la reparación.
examples.en: Therefore, I request the correction of the receipt and payment for the repair.

lessons.title: Flight Rerouted: Text and Call Your Pre-Booked Driver
lessons.objective: Text and call a pre-booked driver to change your pickup time politely, then confirm the new details.

words.note: Mexico: WhatsApp's blue ticks showing a message was read.
Mexico: everyday word for a phone battery.
Prepaid phone credit.
Female cousin; a male cousin is el primo.
Common in polite texts when thanking someone in advance.

words.en: Good afternoon, Don Isidro, I'm writing to let you know about a delay.
words.es: Buenas tardes, don Isidro, le escribo para avisarle de un retraso.
words.note: Formal text opening.

words.en: My connecting flight is leaving 3 hours late.
words.es: Mi vuelo de conexión sale con 3 horas de retraso.

words.en: Could you wait for me at 9:30 instead of 6:30?
words.es: ¿Podría esperarme a las 9:30 en vez de las 6:30?
words.note: The conditional softens the request; formal.

words.en: Sorry, I can't listen to voice notes; could you write to me?
words.es: Disculpe, no puedo escuchar notas de voz; ¿me podría escribir?

words.en: Good afternoon, am I speaking with Don Isidro Martínez?
words.es: Buenas tardes, ¿hablo con don Isidro Martínez?
words.note: Standard way to check who answered the phone.

words.en: Amalia, would you be so kind as to pass the message to your cousin?
words.es: Amalia, ¿sería tan amable de pasarle el mensaje a su primo?
words.note: Formal, usted with someone you don't know.

words.en: I would appreciate it if Don Isidro confirmed by text.
words.es: Le agradecería que don Isidro me confirmara por mensaje.
words.note: This polite request takes the imperfect subjunctive.

words.en: So we're set for 9:30, with the sign at the exit.
words.es: Entonces quedamos a las 9:30, con el letrero en la salida.

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is Isidro Martínez, your pre-booked driver in Oaxaca: text and then call to move your pickup to a new time, using le escribo para avisarle and ¿podría…?, and confirm the new time, the meeting point and your name.

grammar.focus: Phone and text conventions; conditional politeness (le escribo para avisarle, ¿podría esperarme?)

examples.es: Le escribo para avisarle que mi vuelo llega a las 9:30.
examples.en: I'm writing to let you know that my flight arrives at 9:30.

examples.es: ¿Podría decirle a Isidro que me espere en la salida?
examples.en: Could you tell Isidro to wait for me at the exit?

lessons.title: Settle the Week's Bill and Rebook Don Ernesto
lessons.objective: Go through the week's charges with your driver line by line and agree on conditions for hiring him next year.

words.note: Mexico: a simple handwritten bill or receipt.
Each separate charge listed on a bill or invoice.
One line on a bill or page; renglón por renglón means line by line.
Mexico: common everyday way to say next year.

words.en: Don Ernesto, shall we go through the bill line by line?
words.es: Don Ernesto, ¿revisamos la nota renglón por renglón?
words.note: Formal: don + first name with usted.

words.en: Could you explain this waiting charge from Thursday?
words.es: ¿Me podría explicar este cobro por espera del jueves?

words.en: We hadn't agreed on that charge, Don Ernesto.
words.es: Ese cobro no lo habíamos acordado, don Ernesto.

words.en: Apart from that charge, everything else is fine.
words.es: Fuera de ese cargo, todo lo demás está muy bien.

words.en: I would pay for waiting as long as you let me know first.
words.es: Yo pagaría la espera siempre que me avisara antes.
words.note: Conditional + siempre que + imperfect subjunctive.

words.en: I would hire you again as long as you sent me a quote.
words.es: Lo contrataría otra vez con tal de que me mandara una cotización.

words.en: As long as the price is the same, I'll book the same week.
words.es: Siempre que el precio sea el mismo, reservo la misma semana.

words.en: Could you send me the quote on WhatsApp in January?
words.es: ¿Me podría mandar la cotización por WhatsApp en enero?

lessons.speaking: You are the traveler, and the AI is your driver Don Ernesto Lozano in Guadalajara: go through his handwritten bill line by line, question any charge you didn't agree to, and set next year's conditions using the conditional, siempre que and con tal de que.

grammar.focus: Conditional; subjunctive in conditions (siempre que, con tal de que)

examples.es: Lo volvería a contratar siempre que me confirmara el precio por escrito.
examples.en: I would hire you again as long as you confirmed the price in writing.

examples.es: Reservo la misma semana con tal de que la tarifa diaria no cambie.
examples.en: I'll book the same week as long as the daily rate doesn't change.

lessons.title: Capstone: A Long Travel Day Leading a Group in Asunción
lessons.objective: Lead a group through a full day of rides in Spanish, solving problems, keeping everyone safe and reporting it all.

words.note: Paraguay: the usual word for a license plate.
For a woman: la recién llegada.
Paraguay: common word for the car trunk.
Paraguay's currency; prices are often in thousands.

words.en: Fernando, before getting in, ask the driver to say your name.
words.es: Fernando, antes de subir, pedile al conductor que diga tu nombre.
words.note: Informal vos, common in Paraguay.

words.en: Sir, we are 6 and there are only 4 seat belts here; we'll order another car.
words.es: Señor, somos 6 y acá solo hay 4 cinturones; pedimos otro auto.
words.note: Formal, to the driver.

words.en: Wait on the sidewalk until the car has stopped.
words.es: Esperen en la vereda hasta que el auto esté detenido.
words.note: Ustedes command to the group; hasta que + subjunctive.

words.en: No one got hurt, so let's talk about what we'd do differently.
words.es: Nadie se lastimó, así que hablemos de qué haríamos distinto.

words.en: Good afternoon, Nilda, could you change the address for the 7 o'clock pickup?
words.es: Nilda, buenas tardes, ¿podría cambiar la dirección del pedido de las 7?
words.note: Formal, to the dispatcher.

words.en: If the driver arrives early, have him wait for us in the parking lot.
words.es: Si el conductor llega antes, que nos espere en el estacionamiento.

words.en: It should be noted that no one was injured in the hotel incident.
words.es: Cabe señalar que nadie resultó herido en el incidente del hotel.
words.note: Written register for the incident note.

words.en: Therefore, from now on we will always get out on the sidewalk side.
words.es: Por lo tanto, en adelante bajaremos siempre del lado de la vereda.

lessons.speaking: You are the group leader, and the AI is Fernando, your drivers and Nilda at dispatch: coach Fernando on app rides, fix a too-small car, debrief the near miss calmly, call Nilda to change a pickup and dictate the incident note, using commands, si clauses, subjunctive and por lo tanto.

grammar.focus: Capstone: integrating the Master 20 grammar (connectors, commands, subjunctive, si clauses, formal and written register)

examples.es: Si el auto es chico, pidan otro antes de cargar las valijas.
examples.en: If the car is small, order another one before loading the suitcases.

examples.es: Cabe señalar que el conductor frenó a tiempo; por lo tanto, nadie resultó herido.
examples.en: It should be noted that the driver braked in time; therefore, no one was hurt.
